tasks.description: Import random and pick a secret number between 1 and 100. Print 'Game starts!' and the secret (just to test).
tasks.hint:
`import random` at the top.
`random.randint(1, 100)` returns a random integer including both 1 and 100.
Store it: `secret = random.randint(1, 100)` then print it to verify.
tasks.solution:
import random

secret = random.randint(1, 100)
print('Game starts!')
print(secret)
tasks.walkthrough:
`randint(1, 100)` includes both 1 and 100. The secret is stored so later steps can compare against it.
Printing it now is just for testing; you'll remove that line once the game works.

tasks.description: Add a loop: ask the user to guess. Print 'Too low', 'Too high', or 'Correct!' and break when guessed.
tasks.hint:
`while True:` loops forever — use `break` when the player guesses correctly.
Convert input to int: `guess = int(input('Guess: '))`
Three branches: `if guess < secret` → Too low, `elif guess > secret` → Too high, `else` → Correct + break.
tasks.walkthrough:
The loop runs until `break`, which only happens in the `else` branch when the guess matches.
Each guess is converted with `int()` so it can be compared to the number.

tasks.description: Track how many guesses the player took. Print 'You got it in X guesses!' when they win.
tasks.hint:
Create `attempts = 0` before the loop.
Increment inside the loop on each guess: `attempts += 1`
When they win: `print(f'You got it in {attempts} guesses!')`
tasks.solution:
import random

secret = random.randint(1, 100)
attempts = 0
print('Game starts!')

while True:
    guess = int(input('Guess: '))
    attempts += 1
    if guess < secret:
        print('Too low')
    elif guess > secret:
        print('Too high')
    else:
        print(f'You got it in {attempts} guesses!')
        break
tasks.walkthrough:
`attempts` starts at 0 and goes up by one every time a guess is read, before the comparison.
When the guess is right, the message uses the current count.

tasks.description: Add a maximum of 7 guesses. If the player runs out, print 'Game over! The number was X.'
tasks.hint:
Change the while condition: `while attempts < 7:`
After the loop, check if the game was won or lost: `if guess == secret: ...` or use a flag.
If the loop ended without a correct guess: `print(f'Game over! The number was {secret}.')`
tasks.walkthrough:
The loop condition now limits the number of passes to 7.
A `won` flag records whether the loop ended because of a correct guess or because the attempts ran out.
After the loop, the flag decides which message to show.

tasks.description: Wrap the whole game in a function `play_game()`. After it ends, ask 'Play again? (y/n)'. If yes, call the function again.
tasks.hint:
`def play_game():` — move all your game logic inside.
After the function definition: `while True: play_game(); again = input('Play again? (y/n): '); if again != 'y': break`
Or use a while loop: `keep_playing = True` then check the answer.
tasks.walkthrough:
All of the game logic moves inside `play_game()`, indented one level.
The outer loop calls the function, then asks whether to go again. Any answer other than y ends the program.
`.lower()` means Y and y both work.

lesson.intro:
Your first full program: a guessing game. You'll build it in five small steps,
each adding one feature. Every step should run on its own before you move to
the next. That habit, small working steps, is the most useful thing to take from
this day.

sections.heading: Step 1: a secret number
sections.body:
`random.randint(1, 100)` picks the secret. Print it while you're building so
you can test quickly, then remove that print at the end.
sections.code:
import random

secret = random.randint(1, 100)
print('Game starts!')
print(f'(psst, it is {secret})')

sections.heading: Step 2: the guessing loop
sections.body:
A `while True` loop that asks for a guess, compares it with the secret, and
breaks when they match. Three outcomes means `if`/`elif`/`else`.
sections.output:
Guess: Too low
Guess: Too high
Guess: Correct!

sections.heading: Step 3 and 4: counting and limiting attempts
sections.body:
A counter that starts at 0 and goes up once per guess. To cap the attempts,
change the loop condition to `while attempts < 7` and, after the loop, work
out whether they won. A `won` flag keeps that check simple.
sections.code:
secret = 42
attempts = 0
won = False
while attempts < 7:
    guess = int(input('Guess: '))
    attempts += 1
    if guess == secret:
        won = True
        break
    print('Too low' if guess < secret else 'Too high')

if won:
    print(f'You got it in {attempts} guesses!')
else:
    print(f'Game over! The number was {secret}.')
sections.output:
Guess: Too low
Guess: You got it in 2 guesses!

sections.heading: Step 5: play again
sections.body:
Move the whole game into a function, then loop: play, ask, repeat if yes.
Notice how the function makes this trivial: the game is just one call.
sections.output:
(a whole game happens here)
Play again? (y/n): Thanks for playing

watch_out: Comparing the guess as a string. `input()` gives text; convert with `int()` before comparing to the number.
Incrementing `attempts` inside the `if` instead of once per loop pass.
Testing with a random secret is slow. Temporarily set `secret = 42` while you build.
In this app, put each guess on its own line in the input box before running.
